Based on the web search results, here's what I found about the SOLIDGEO benchmark:

## SOLIDGEO Overview

SolidGeo is the first large-scale benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the performance of MLLMs on mathematical reasoning tasks in solid geometry. SolidGeo consists of 3,113 real-world K–12 and competition-level problems, each paired with visual context and annotated with difficulty levels and fine-grained solid geometry categories.

## Scope and Coverage

The benchmark covers a wide range of 3D reasoning subjects such as projection, unfolding, spatial measurement, and spatial vector, offering a rigorous testbed for assessing solid geometry.

The dataset is categorized into eight fine-grained domains: Composite Solid Structures, Spatial Metric Relations, Solid Shape Identification, Planar Unfolding and Configuration, Measurement of Solid Geometric Forms, Solid Geometry Modeling, Multi-view Projection, and 3D Coordinate and Vector Reasoning.

## Motivation and Findings

Existing multimodal mathematics benchmarks mainly focus on plane geometry and largely ignore solid geometry, which requires spatial reasoning and is more challenging than plane geometry.

Through extensive experiments, MLLMs encounter substantial challenges in solid geometry math tasks, with a considerable performance gap relative to human capabilities on SolidGeo.

## Presentation

The work was presented at the 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks.
